items.title: Centered smooth-plus-homogeneous objectives
items.note: centered states the theorem with all hypotheses written out: F convex, x_* a minimizer, U open and convex, ψ convex and locally C^{1,1} on U (LocallyC11On U ψ: differentiable on U with locally Lipschitz derivative), γ finite convex positively homogeneous of degree one, F = ψ + γ(· - x_*) on U (disp/010), and every admissible run whose initial sublevel {F ≤ F(x_0)} is compact and contained in U; conclusion: F(x_k) → F(x_*), Euclidean dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0, and x_k → x_* if x_* is the unique minimizer. The last sentence ("Neither original summand is required to be minimized at x_*") is centered_summands_not_minimized: an instance of all hypotheses in which neither ψ nor γ(· - x_*) is minimized at x_*. The proof follows the paper (via the inward condition and Corollary art:radial-convergence); the library's centered_values/centered_iterates prove the value and iterate statements by a cocoercivity bound instead.
Hypothesis hrep : ∀ x ∈ U, F x = ψ x + γ (x - xstar).

The steps are stated in Lean: initial_value_gt (F(x_0) > F(x_*)), uniform_lipschitz_gradient (a uniform Lipschitz constant on the compact convex K), the display (smooth_inward_remainder), homogeneous_part_at_differentiable and the Euler identity, centered_inward_condition (M_eta = L max_K ||r_x||^2, theta_eta = 1/2) and Corollary art:radial-convergence.

Stated under the theorem's hypotheses, for an admissible run with compact initial sublevel in U, K = {F ≤ F(x_0)} (variable with its defining equation) and a uniform Euclidean Lipschitz constant L ≥ 0 of ∇ψ (coordinateGradient ψ) on K, at every x ∈ K and every 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1 (the whole inward segment [x, x_*] ⊆ K). The Lean proof bounds the derivative of the remainder along the segment by Lτ‖r_x‖² (Mathlib's image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary) instead of integrating.
mixed_hypotheses: psi(u,v) = u^2, gamma(u,v) = |v|, x_* = 0, U = R^2 satisfy all hypotheses of Theorem art:centered, with compact sublevels and a unique minimizer; mixed_benchmark is proved this way.

The homogeneous terms ||Ax||_1 and max_i a_i^Tx are finite, convex and positively homogeneous of degree one, so Theorem art:centered applies to psi + gamma(. - x_*) with these gamma. The local active-sign splitting for the Lasso is Corollary art:local-centered (Section art:local).

items.anchor: When $\psi=0$, the inward remainder vanishes everywhere on $\R^n$.
items.note: ψ = 0 in Theorem art:centered: the inward remainder of a finite convex positively homogeneous F toward 0 vanishes, so art:inward-condition holds with M_η = 0 on every sublevel.

items.anchor: coercivity prevents rays of zero or negative slope
items.note: Coercive homogeneous F has F(0) = 0 and F > 0 off zero (no ray of zero or negative slope), and with F(x) >= mu||x|| (display A/global/disp/013) F(x_k) -> 0 implies x_k -> 0, for every admissible run.

"It" is coercivity, together with the other hypotheses of Theorem art:homogeneous (finite, convex, positively homogeneous of degree one). Witnesses that these force neither property: the ℓ¹ norm on R² satisfies all hypotheses and is not differentiable at (1, 0) ≠ 0; the Euclidean norm on R² satisfies all hypotheses and is not a finite maximum of linear forms ("finite-piece" read as finitely many linear pieces, the finite linear maxima of the section). Both are covered by the theorem (l1_norm_case, euclidean_norm_case). Consistent with prose/027.

items.title: Coercive positively homogeneous objectives
items.note: Hypotheses 1 ≤ n, F convex (finite), Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne F, coercive = Tendsto F (cocompact (Vec n)) atTop. Conclusion: 0 minimizes F and every minimizer is 0, and every R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F (arbitrary x_0, H_0, c_1, c_2: the last sentence of the theorem) has F(x_k) → 0 and x_k → 0 (disp/012). Proved as in the paper through Theorem art:centered with ψ = 0, γ = F; the library proves the iterate statement through the homogeneous potential. Not vacuous: absRun (built by oneDimRun) is an explicit admissible run on the coercive homogeneous F(x) = |x| on R (x_k = (-1/2)^k, H_k = (3/2)2^{-k}, α_k = 1, c_1 = 1/4, c_2 = 1/2); see the module's non-vacuity example.

homogeneous is proved along this proof: coercive_homogeneous_positive (lines 235-237: F(0) = 0 and F > 0 off zero), sphere_minimum and homogeneous_sphere_bound (disp/013: μ = min over the Euclidean unit sphere > 0, F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖), sublevels_compact_of_coercive (line 242), Theorem art:centered with x_* = 0, U = ℝⁿ, ψ = 0, γ = F (lines 243-244), iterates_of_values (line 244: F(x_k) ≥ μ‖x_k‖ gives x_k → 0). homogeneous_inward_condition (M_η = 0) and homogeneous_via_radial state the radial route of the October text (the inward remainder is identically zero, so Corollary art:radial-convergence applies directly), which the current proof no longer takes; both are kept and remain correct. All steps hold as written.

Under the theorem's hypotheses: the minimum of F over the Euclidean unit sphere {‖euclideanVector x‖ = 1} exists (IsLeast of the image), and the minimum μ satisfies μ > 0 and F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖ for all x. The facts F(0) = 0 and F > 0 off zero, proved before the display, are derived rather than assumed.

items.title: Norms, gauges, and coercive linear maxima
items.note: One theorem per case, each with the conclusion of Theorem art:homogeneous (0 is the unique minimizer; every admissible run, from every admissible start, has F(x_k) → 0 and x_k → 0) in its setting n ≥ 1. Norm: N : Seminorm ℝ (Vec n) with N x = 0 → x = 0. Gauge: F convex, PositiveDegreeOne, {F ≤ 1} bounded. Linear maximum (disp/013): a : Fin m → Vec n and F x the greatest of the a_iᵀx (IsGreatest of the range; no affine intercepts), {F ≤ 0} bounded. BfgsArticle.HomogeneousModels states the same three cases (norm_conclusion, gauge_conclusion, finiteMaxLinear_conclusion, with a Finset of slopes). Not vacuous: |x| on R is a norm, a gauge with bounded unit sublevel and the linear maximum max(x, -x), and absRun is an admissible run for it (also as normSeminorm ℝ (Vec 1)).

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M39): end-of-proof mark. The three cases are proved along this proof: positivity off zero (norm axioms; for the gauge and the maximum, boundedness of the stated sublevel via Homogeneous.positive_of_bounded_zero_sublevel, the ray argument), sphere_minimum and coercive_of_lower_bound (F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖, hence coercivity), maxLinear_convex_homogeneous (finite maxima of linear forms are finite, convex and degree-one homogeneous), then Theorem art:homogeneous. All hold as written.

l1: on {x_i = 0} the norm along e_i is ||x||_1 + |t|, so it is not differentiable there (l1_nonsmooth). l-infinity: at x with |x_i| = |x_j| = max_k |x_k| > 0, i != j, the norm is not differentiable (linf_nonsmooth, linf_tie_example).

The Euclidean norm and |x| on R are instances of the norm case; asymmetric_example: F(x) = max(x, -2x) on R satisfies the hypotheses of the gauge and max-linear cases without symmetry. The attributions to [GL18, Corollary 4.2] and [LO, Section 5.1] are not checked.

In Theorem art:failure_polyhedral the affine piece v - 17 moves the minimizer to (-1,16) while the run converges to the nonstationary origin; a coercive linear maximum without intercepts is covered by Theorem art:homogeneous.

Dichotomy F(x_k) → 0 or F(x_k) → -∞ for every admissible run of a finite convex positively homogeneous F; bounded below ⇒ 0 minimizes F and F(x_k) → 0; the iterate consequence stated is bounded zero sublevel ⇒ x_k → 0 ("additional iterate consequences" is not specific; the companion chapter has more). The attribution to Chapter 7 is checked by the companion register (C_07_H). Runs on homogeneous objectives exist (absRun, asymRun).
